params.body:
**Triage proposal** (from the forwarded mail; change the labels if it is wrong)
Category: bug  Priority: P1
Summary: A team member who was given the editor role in Accounts still cannot edit posts outside their own. A role change only counts after the next sign-in, so the editor role (#384) does nothing for someone already signed in.

**What happens.** The role a request acts with comes from the sign-in token, not from the users table. `getRequestUser` (`packages/server/auth.mjs`) returns the token payload as signed, and `GET /auth/verify`, which the Studio calls on load to learn who is signed in, echoes the same payload. A token lives seven days. So when an admin changes someone's role in Accounts, both the API (`mayEdit`) and the Studio's `canEdit` keep using the old role until that person signs out and in again, or the token runs out.

That holds both ways: a promotion to editor or admin does not count yet, and neither does a demotion to client. A removal already counts at once, because `isDisabled` looks the account up on every request.

**Seen in.** An editor role was given after #384 was deployed. The person reported back that the same posts still cannot be edited.

**Expected.** A role changed in Accounts counts on the next request, the way a removal already does.

Source: Portal mail:33.
params.title: A role changed in Accounts only counts after the next sign-in
